steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 2 9x5-inch loaf pans. In a bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, and salt.

In a separate large bowl, beat the butter, vegetable shortening, white sugar, and brown sugar together with an electric mixer on Low until thoroughly mixed; beat in the bananas, eggs, buttermilk, sour cream, and vanilla extract until well combined. Mix half of the flour mixture into the banana mixture; beat until combined; beat in remaining flour mixture. Mix on Medium speed for 1 minute. Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the loaves comes out clean, 50 minutes to 1 hour. Allow to cool for 15 minutes; serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Angie's To-Die-For Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: Tender banana bread is made with sour cream and buttermilk for richness. This recipe contains no nuts. Serve it warm with butter.

video.description: Beautiful banana bread that is sure to be one of the ultimate comfort foods after you try this recipe out!

review.reviewBody: Awesome banana bread, and yes this recipe is "To-Die-For"! I know that may seem a bit overly dramatic, but this stuff is really good. I've made a lot of banana breads on this site and this is one of the better recipes. I cut the recipe in half as I only needed one bread but I wish I'd made two! I used butter-flavored shortening, added a little more banana, and used low-fat buttermilk and sour cream. I did add a bit of cinnamon and next time I think I might add in some walnuts or chocolate chips - and believe me there will definitely be a next time! This bread was very moist (ya just gotta love baking with buttermilk), rich and delicious. Oh so good warm out of the oven with a bit of butter. Thanks for a great recipe AMHORSCH!

I made this yesterday and it turned out quite nicely. I had some sour cream and buttermilk that I needed to use up, and so this fit the bill perfectly. I had to cook mine a bit longer than what the recipe says to cook it for (about 20 minutes more). The top started browning too much, so I tented the loaves with some foil as they finished baking. They came out great! I added 3/4 of a cup of semisweet chocolate chips and 3/4 of a cup of chopped walnuts just to give it some extra pizzazz. We live at high altitude (6,000 ft), so I never know how my baked goods are going to turn out when I try something for the first time, but these rose beautifully. No sinking or anything. Thanks for a great recipe, AMHORSCH! We really enjoyed it!

Very moist cake. Really enjoyed the banana flavor. There was plenty of batter left over after filling two large loaf pans, so I made a dozen muffins as well. My grandson wouldn't stop eating them! I've been making a banana bread recipe for over 30 years from a cookbook of my mother's that she got as a gift when she married my father. It served me well over the years, but this one was so full of flavor and so much easier to make that it will be my go-to recipe for banana bread from now on. 
Thank you very much for your contribution!

FOLLOWUP:
It's been 6 months since my first review, and I'm still getting requests for this banana bread from my family & friends. As fantastic as it is, I've also put my personal spin on it. I've substituted Greek yogurt for the sour cream because it's creamier & has less fat content. I prefer to sour milk I have on hand with vinegar rather than wasting my money to buy buttermilk at the market. I use 5 bananas instead of four & pour all of the batter into a 9 x 13 pan & bake for 60 minutes. (Even better when I make a double batch & bake with two 9x13 pans!) I use my eggs at room temperature to make a lighter, less dense cake. I like the glossy appearance of the cake once it's baked. So very tasty!
Thank you again Angie, for sharing this wonderful recipe!

Thank you for posting this recipe! I recently threw my favorite recipe away while writing new recipe cards. I love a banana bread that uses buttermilk and sour cream. Here is my cooking notes: added 2 tsp. cinnamon, 1c. semi-sweet chocolate chunks, 1 1/2 c. walnut halves. Used all butter for the fat. no shortening. Cut sugar by 1/2c. and used 5 large banana's. recipe made 2 large loaves. cook time in my oven @350* was 75 min. Loaves were tented at 52 minutes. color was a beautiful medium caramel color. I have not tasted since they are still cooling down. will repost once tasted. Thank you once again! UPDATE: Taste is Excellent! Recipe is a keeper and will definitely make again. Thankfully, I found another go to Banana Bread recipe. Bon Apetit !

To die for......yes, ma'am! I made this today with my older boy only substituting whole wheat white flour for the regular flour and cutting the white sugar back to a scant 1/2 cup. I made 12 large-ish muffins for us as snacks and three "gift" loaves for friends (random acts of kindness!). This banana bread is one of the best we've ever had. Really, REALLY to die for! I hate to make it lighter because it's really freaking yummy but next time, I might cut the butter and oil back by half and add more mashed banana. NOTE: To prevent a tough banana bread, I always wisk together all my dry ingredients (including sugar) and all my wet ingredients and then fold the dry into the wet until just moistened making sure not to overmix. You get perfect quick bread/muffins every time. EDITED: I've now made this recipe twice and not only does my family love it, but so do the six people we've made gift loaves for. Thanks!

I was a little nervous about being the first to make muffins with this recipe, but I don't have a loaf pan, so I did! 18 minutes in a pan prepped with cooking spray was perfect. I sprinkled them with rolled oats. To-Die-For indeed! The recipe will make about 36 muffins. :)
Love this recipe. I made mini muffins and baked for 10 min at 350. Perfect!!! They were very good, light and moist. I will be making these again!!

My oven temp is off which is why the bread is darker than it should be. It is delicious, soft and moist! I can definitely see making 3 loaves out of this recipe. These are large loaves and one has been partiality eaten! Banana flavor is good, sweet, but not overly sweet. You can definitely reduce sugar in this recipe if you like and I don’t think it would be any issue. I would make this again in a heart beat. I didn’t have buttermilk so I used unsweetened almond milk and French vanilla refrigerated coffee creamer and a splash of lemon juice.

The bread is just as good as everyone has described it. Like some previous reviews, it yields quite a bit of batter. I used two loaf pans and used a small Pyrex glass bowl for the rest of the batter and baked it. I used 1 cup of butter instead of shortening. I found that the top of bread was crispy and I know it’s because of the butter. Also I used one cup brown one cup white and eliminated the extra sugar and it was sweet enough for me.

Okay, so I only had one loaf pan (not sure where that second one went) so I had to get creative with the 20 other pans I have. Using round cake pans didn't seem right and I didn't want to make mini loaves or cupcakes. Aha, there's my trusty Bundt pan. Still an odd choice but it made the most sense. She worked like a charm. I did have to cook it longer, 70 mins to be exact. The bread turned out beautiful and very tasty. It had a wonderful crust on top and once out of the pan and cooled the outside crisped up nicely. I will definitely be making this again, loafed or Bundted.

7.2.12 ... https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/216774/angies-to-die-for-banana-bread/ ... Yes, agreed, uh-huh, very good. 'Reduced white sugar by a half & used an additional banana.Added a little vanilla, too.Very moist.I also substituted a cup & a half soy yogurt for the buttermilk & sour cream.They didn't need the additional fat from either.I made twelve muffins & two 8x4 loaves.'Not so sure that much batter would fit in two 9x5s as the recipe states.In the bread I put a layer of fresh blueberries.'Not so pretty, but good, too.I also like banana bread 8 & 4.Later: Ya know, I think it may be too moist.'Think I'll try reducing the shortening.It didn't last long enough to happen, but with quickbread getting that sticky top anyway plus being extramoist, 'seems you're inviting an early mold. (Sorry to bring that up with a good recipe!) Note: Was years between making this & other two I liked (Deborah Stone-Gove & Teri Lynn), but I think I liked theirs better.
Even better with chopped walnuts! This is the best recipe I have found.

I wanted to try this recipe because it wasn't like the standard banana bread better that is usually made. It was definitely a winner in my book. It had a nice deep golden brown crust that was sweet and the inside was spongy and more like a cake than a bread. It was moist and delicate with some hints of caramelization and salt. I was also surprised at the various fats and acids were used. It made the flavors deeper and more complex. I didn't do anything different except cut the recipe in half and baked the bread at 350° for 1 hour. The spread is amazing, thank you very much!
It is litteretly "to die for".
I have made this recipe several times, no additions needed. It's a wonderful moist banana bread!
More ingredients than most banana breads I've tried, but it was delicious and I loved that it makes two loaves. I would recommend using your largest mixing bowl because it is a large batter.
The recipe is perfect! The best I've made so far.
makes two very large loafs-my pans were to small-not alot of bananna flavor
No changes @ all. This is the best ever. We loved it!
Wow. This is really an awesome recipe. By far the best banana loaf. Will definitely make again and again. Thank You for sharing.
